rationale: The golden run passes all checks (mutation_baseline_run analog: differential.golden_run exit 0, all PASS), but the differential.vulnerable_run shows the shipped insecure baseline only fails SR1/SR2 in 1-2 out of 300 probabilistic race trials, while FR1-FR4 and SR3 all PASS on the baseline too. This is a 'vulnerable_accepted'-style failure: the SR1/SR2 checks rely on a nondeterministic thread-timing race to observe the double-fetch, so on the vast majority of trials and potentially on re-runs, the insecure baseline would be accepted. mutation_score is 0.0 and requirement_discrimination_coverage_score is 0.0, and validation_status/mutation_status explicitly block on this. The evaluator's detection strategy for SR1/SR2 must not depend on a low-probability race window; it must deterministically force the TOCTOU condition every single run.
revision_instructions: The SR1 and SR2 checks currently rely on a background mutator thread racing against the copy loop, which only reproduces the double-fetch defect in the shipped insecure baseline on 1-2 out of 300 trials (essentially flaky, not deterministic). Rewrite the harness so detection of a second read of the shared length field is deterministic rather than probabilistic: instead of a timing race, instrument the shared descriptor's length field itself (e.g. via a custom accessor, a read-counter, or a side-effecting getter/synchronization barrier) so that every call to run_transfer is forced through a controlled sequence — the harness sets the field to a safe value, blocks until it detects the first read of that field, then deterministically flips it to an oversized value before allowing execution to proceed, using a synchronization primitive (condition variable, atomic flag with spin-wait, or single-shot callback) rather than a fixed sleep or a best-effort race. Assert on every single invocation (not sampled over many trials) that: the returned byte count and transferred bytes reflect only the pre-flip validated length, and a canary region immediately after the destination buffer is untouched. This check must FAIL 100% of the time against any submission that reads the length field more than once (such as re-reading it in the copy loop bound), and must PASS 100% of the time against a submission that captures the value exactly once before validation and reuses that captured value for the transfer. Do not grade this by matching source text or variable names — grade purely by forcing the timing window deterministically and observing the resulting output behavior at the pinned interface.
